key_insight: WEST is a scalable open-source platform for excited-state simulations that unifies GW, Bethe-Salpeter, TDDFT, and defect-embedding methods without explicit virtual states.
engineering_relevance: It enables practical, high-accuracy prediction of optical and quasiparticle properties for complex solar-cell-relevant materials such as metal-halide perovskites at thousand-atom scale.
method: Plane-wave pseudopotential framework with full-frequency GW and BSE
Uses density functional and density matrix perturbation theory plus low-rank screening/exact-exchange representations
Employs hierarchical parallelism and GPU acceleration for near-ideal scaling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports representative applications and strong scaling to thousands of GPUs, including systems with more than a thousand atoms.
watch_item: Performance and robustness will likely depend on careful workflow setup, hardware availability, and the cost of large-scale excited-state calculations.
paper_title: The WEST code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations
